in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi there! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 6 years old. I'm wondering if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad. But I still support Alex financially - does that matter?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, where you live does matter for Child Benefit eligibility. Since you're living abroad, there are specific rules that apply.

Can you tell me which country you're currently living in? Also, are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain. And no, I'm not a Crown servant - I'm not with the armed forces or anything like that. I moved here for work.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since you're living in Spain and are not a Crown servant, that affects your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To complete my assessment, I need to ask: Where does Alex live? Does he live with you in Spain, or does he live in the UK with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives in the UK with his mum - my ex-partner. He doesn't live with me in Spain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

- You live in Spain (not in the UK)

- Alex lives in the UK with his mum (your ex-partner)
- You provide financial support to Alex

conversation.text:
**Assessment Result: Not Eligible**

I'm sorry, but you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex while you're living in Spain.

Here's why:

The main requirement for Child Benefit is that you must live in the UK. You may be able to claim if you live abroad only in specific circumstances - such as being a Crown servant (diplomat, armed forces member posted abroad) or living in certain countries with special arrangements.

Since you're living in Spain for work and are not a Crown servant, you don't meet the UK residence requirement.

Additionally, only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child. Since Alex lives in the UK with his mother, she would be the appropriate person to claim Child Benefit for him if she hasn't already done so.

Even though you're providing financial support to Alex (which is commendable), this doesn't change the residence requirement for claiming Child Benefit.
